newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-JONES, GILDER TIED FOR LEAD AT KAPULUA INTERNATIONAL.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-JONES, GILDER TIED FOR LEAD AT KAPULUA INTERNATIONAL.

text.p: U.S. Open champion Steve Jones and former champion Bob Gilder tied a course record with nine-under-par 64s Thursday and shared a one-shot lead after the opening round of the $1.1 million Kapulua International.

Jones and Gilder played the par-73 Plantation Course and tied the mark set last year by Davis Love. Alone in third place was two-time former champion Fred Couples. His eight-under 63 at the Bay Course was one stroke off the course record set last year by Mike Sullivan.
The Kapalua International is not an official PGA event and the top five players on the PGA money list skipped it, as did 20-year-old sensation Tiger Woods.
Kirk Triplett and Mike Hulbert had seven-under 64s on the Bay Course and were two shots behind Jones, whose one-stroke victory at the U.S. Open was his first since 1989.

Jones had back-to-back birdies at the second and third holes and ran off three more beginning with a four-footer at the fifth hole. He completed a 30 on the front nine with a birdie at the par-five ninth hole.

Jones barely missed birdie putts at 10 and 11 before rolling in a 10-footer at the 12th hole that moved him to seven under. He picked up his other birdies at 15, where he two-putted from 30 feet, and 18. Jones birdied all four par-fives.
"Anytime you shoot nine under, you are pleased," he said. "It could have been real good. All of my putts were within makeable conditions.
"I shot 73 in the first round last year, so this is an improvement," Jones added. "I like it here. No pressure, I just play. I'm looking forward to playing this time of year."
Gilder, who won here in 1988, moved into a tie for the lead by birdying the 18th hole.

Couples is seeking his first win since the Players Championship last March. He played the back nine first and had four birdies and a bogey before making the turn. Couples sank a five-foot eagle putt on the par-five first hole, then ran off four straight pars before birdying three of the last four holes.
"Some of the easier shots, I didn't hit good," he said. "I need to loosen up, stretch and go walk."
Clarence Rose, Tim Herron, Scott McCarron and Roger Maltbie had six-under 67s at Plantation and were three strokes off the pace.
Defending champion Jim Furyk was five shots behind the leaders after an opening-round 67 at the Bay Course.
The Plantation Course is a par-73 that measures 7,263 yards, while the Bay Course is a par-71, 6,600-yard layout. First prize is $198,000.
